strategyPosture: Stay constructive but selective: credit (HY OAS 3.12%, SLOOS 0%) and the index (SPY -0.5% from high) do not confirm the hike-cycle or rollover narratives, while the actionable edge sits in RESEARCH_SCREENED, sentiment-driven dislocations where revenue growth (+55% AVGO, +27.7% VRT) contradicts price — research first, size only after 1-month trends stop falling.

themes.counterRead: Credit is not confirming a rollover — HY OAS is 3.12% and SLOOS is 0% — so treat Mag7 weakness as rotation inside a still-supported index, not as a short-the-index signal. The risk is asymmetric the other way: if lending standards tighten toward 40% while the -8.84-point gap widens, the rotation read flips to a rollover read.
themes.dataAnchor: Market concentration reads ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: the Mag7 average sits -9.34% from its 52-week high, a -8.84-point divergence gap versus SPY, with TSLA weakest at -24.5% and AAPL strongest at -2.4%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, well below the ~40% stress threshold), and small caps confirm rotation rather than broad risk appetite: IWM is -5.68% over 1 month and -1.22% today versus QQQ +5.33% over 1 month.
themes.label: Index Leadership Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY at 777.21, only -0.5% from its 52-week high and +1.47% over 1 month — so the surface read is that nothing has changed in leadership.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS rising toward the ~40% stress threshold or the Mag7-vs-SPY divergence gap widening beyond -8.84 points would flip this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: Equities priced at the highs against a 5.28% 10-year and a 2.92% real yield leave no cushion if the hike narrative becomes actual tightening — the calm in VIX (15.15) and HY OAS (3.12%) is the market pricing the narrative as talk. Posture should respect that the first of those two gauges to move, not the headlines, is the real signal.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve is steep and high: DGS2 4.84%, DGS10 5.28%, DGS30 5.67%, 2s10s +0.44, real 10y 2.92% with T10YIE at 2.36% and DFF at 3.88%. Yet stress gauges disagree with the bite narrative: HY OAS is only 3.12% and VIX is 15.15 (-3.63% over 1 month), while SPY holds -0.5% from its 52-week high.
themes.label: 5%+ Long Yields, Unstressed Credit
themes.narrative: Active FOMC event signals (HIGH strength, 7 hits each for the Sep, Oct and Dec meetings) carry a rate-hike-cycle narrative, with the Fed putting AI on its list of inflation shocks — the implied belief is that restrictive policy is about to bite risk assets.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS widening above its current 3.12% or VIX sustaining above 15.15 alongside a DGS10 move beyond 5.28% would confirm the hike narrative is becoming a liquidity event.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals ahead of price is the opportunity setup, but depth alone is not the trigger: several of these names are still falling over 1 month (APP -10.9%, KTOS -13.4%, BWXT -11%), so the data supports research and staged interest, not chasing the deepest discount. AVGO's combination of the highest score (81) and a non-oversold RSI (57.3) makes it the cleanest expression; the oversold names (TTD RSI 30.2, KTOS 32.4) need a trend stop first.
themes.dataAnchor: The screener's top conviction name is AVGO (score 81, Tier A): revenue growing 55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M FCF (42.1% margin) while the stock sits -24.6% from its high at RSI 57.3. The same pattern repeats down the list — VRT revenue +27.7% at -35.8% from high, NXT revenue +20.3% at -47.6%, BWXT revenue +18.3% at -41% — and the pullback posture is RESEARCH_SCREENED across all candidates.
themes.label: Sentiment-Driven Dislocations in Growing Names
themes.narrative: Price action says the growth complex is broken: 23 tracked dislocations are classified SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, with names like KTOS -68.9%, APP -62.3% and HUBS -55.7% from their 52-week highs.
themes.watchFor: A dislocation name whose 1-month trend turns positive while it remains more than 20% below its 52-week high — e.g. NOW already at +3.8% 1-month and -27.8% from high — confirms the sentiment washout is ending.

themes.counterRead: The unwind is concentrated in the speculative, pre-revenue leg (SMR, OKLO) while contracted power (VST) holds and a moat supplier (BWXT) screens as recovery — the theme narrative ran ahead of fundamentals in the speculative names, which is caution there, not a reason to abandon the complex. VST itself is extended short-term (RSI 75.3), so the data favors the beaten-down supplier over chasing the leader.
themes.dataAnchor: The 1-month tape splits it in two: SMR -33.27%, URA -16.14%, OKLO -15.72% and CCJ -12.28% are the market's worst laggards, all down again today (-3.84% to -6.98%), while VST is +9.1% over 1 month and +3.13% today. Underneath, BWXT is a watchlist promotion (score 76, revenue growing 26.1% YoY, RECOVERY inflection) at -41% from its high and $142.76.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power: Speculative Leg Unwinding, Contracted Leg Holding
themes.narrative: The nuclear and AI-power trade still reads as one theme in headlines, implying the whole complex should move together on structural power demand.
themes.watchFor: SMR stabilizing after its -33.27% 1-month fall, or VST's RSI cooling from 75.3 while holding above its 1-month gains, would signal the split is resolving rather than spreading.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move most likely builds in the dislocation list, not the index leaders: names like NOW (+3.8% 1-month, -27.8% from high) and CLS (+12.9% trend in dislocations, revenue +28.5%) show the washout already turning, and a positive 1-month turn in the deeper names (AVGO, VRT, NXT) is the trigger that promotes the theme.
